paraphrases: If I play a unit to a battlefield I already control, does that make it Contested?
My opponent already controls a battlefield and I move a unit there — is it Contested now?
Does moving a unit onto a battlefield its controller already controls apply Contested status?
explanation: No — moving a unit onto a battlefield its controller already controls does not make it Contested. Contested status only applies when a unit's controller does NOT already control the battlefield it's moving to: "Units moving to or being played to a battlefield apply Contested status if that battlefield is not already Contested and that Unit's controller does not already control that battlefield." Here the controller already controls the battlefield, so that second condition is false and Contested is never applied.

paraphrases: If I play a unit to a battlefield I don't control, and it isn't already Contested, does that make it Contested?
A battlefield isn't Contested and I don't control it — if I move a unit there, does it become Contested?
explanation: Yes — that battlefield becomes Contested. Contested status applies "if that battlefield is not already Contested and that Unit's controller does not already control that battlefield." Both parts of that condition are true in this situation (it isn't already Contested, and you don't already control it), so moving your unit there applies Contested status to it.

paraphrases: If a battlefield is already Contested and another unit moves there, does that apply Contested again?
Does moving a second unit to an already-Contested battlefield contest it a second time?
explanation: No — a second unit moving to a battlefield that's already Contested doesn't apply Contested again. The rule that grants Contested status explicitly requires "that battlefield is not already Contested"; since it already is, that condition isn't met, so this move doesn't trigger anything new (the battlefield simply stays Contested from whatever originally applied it).

paraphrases: If I have Tank on my unit, do spells from enemies have to target me first as well?
Does Tank on my unit force enemy spells to target it before other units?
My unit has Tank — does that make it a required target for enemy spells too?
explanation: No — Tank has nothing to do with spell targeting. Tank only governs combat damage assignment priority: it's "functionally short for 'I must be assigned lethal damage before any other unit with the same controller as me that does not have [Tank] during the Combat Damage step.'" That's specifically about how a player assigns COMBAT damage during the Combat Damage step — it doesn't require enemy spells to target that unit at all. Whether a spell can target it depends entirely on that spell's own targeting text, not on Tank.

paraphrases: If a unit has Tank twice, does that do anything extra?
Does having two instances of Tank on the same unit stack?
explanation: No — multiple instances of Tank on the same unit are redundant. Having Tank twice doesn't do anything a single instance of Tank doesn't already do.

paraphrases: If a unit is Exhausted, can a spell that can only target Ready units target it?
My unit is Exhausted — can an enemy spell that requires targeting a Ready unit target it?
explanation: No — a spell that can only target Ready units can't target an Exhausted one. Exhausted and Ready are the two states a Game Object can be in for these purposes; a unit that's Exhausted isn't Ready, so it doesn't meet a spell's requirement to target only Ready units.

paraphrases: If I exhaust a unit that's already exhausted, does anything happen?
Can I exhaust a unit that is already exhausted?
explanation: No — nothing extra happens. A Game Object that's already Exhausted can't be Exhausted again, and if something instructs it to be Exhausted anyway, that instruction just does nothing additional.

paraphrases: If I stun a unit that's already stunned, does anything extra happen?
Can a Stunned unit be Stunned again?
explanation: No — a unit that's already Stunned can't be Stunned again. Attempting to stun it a second time doesn't do anything further, and abilities that specifically trigger "when you stun" a unit won't trigger from that redundant attempt either.

paraphrases: If a spell is countered, does it still deal its damage?
If Defy counters a spell, does that countered spell still deal its damage?
Does a countered card or ability still resolve its effect?
explanation: No — a countered spell does nothing at all, including not dealing its damage. A card or ability that's Countered "does nothing and is cleared from the chain" — it's removed before it ever resolves, so none of its effects (damage included) happen.

paraphrases: If my spell gets countered, do I get its costs back?
Does countering a card refund the costs paid to play it?
explanation: No — countering never refunds costs. Whatever you paid to play the card, activate the ability, or trigger the ability stays paid even though the card or ability itself does nothing once countered.

paraphrases: If a spell is countered, does it still count as being played for other abilities that trigger on spells being played?
Does a countered card still trigger 'whenever you play a spell' abilities?
explanation: No — a countered card isn't considered to have been played at all for that purpose. Other abilities that trigger specifically on cards being played won't trigger off a card that ends up Countered.

paraphrases: Does marked damage on a unit reduce its Might?
If a unit has damage marked on it, does that lower its Might stat?
My unit has 5 Might and 3 damage marked on it — is its Might now 2?
Does taking damage permanently weaken a unit's Might?
If my unit has damage on it already, is its printed Might still accurate?
Does damage marked on a unit get subtracted from its Might when checking abilities that care about Might?
explanation: No — marked damage doesn't reduce a unit's Might. Might and marked damage are two separate, independently-tracked values. Lethal Damage — the amount that will kill the unit — is defined as "a non-zero amount greater than or equal to that Unit's Might," meaning damage is compared against the unit's Might to determine when it dies, not subtracted from the Might number itself. A unit with 5 Might and 3 damage marked on it still has 5 Might; it just needs 2 more marked damage to reach lethal.

paraphrases: If a unit gains Shield from two different sources, do the Shield values add up?
Does Shield stack when a unit is granted it by more than one source?
explanation: Yes — Shield values from multiple sources add together. If a unit already has Shield and gains it from an additional source, the granted Shield Values are summed rather than one replacing the other.

paraphrases: If my deck runs out of cards, do I lose the game immediately?
What happens if I have to draw and my Main Deck is empty?
Does running out of cards in my deck cause an instant loss?
explanation: No — running out of cards doesn't cause an instant loss. Instead, you Burn Out: you recycle your trash back into your Main Deck (randomizing it), give an opponent 1 point, and then complete whatever action caused you to run out (such as drawing the card you needed). If your trash is also empty, this repeats — you keep giving away points each time — until an opponent's points reach the win threshold, at which point they win. There's no separate "deck-out" loss condition; it's all handled through this point-scoring loop.

paraphrases: If I have two sources of Vision, do they trigger separately?
Do multiple instances of Vision each trigger on their own?
explanation: Yes — each instance of Vision triggers on its own. Having two sources of Vision means you get two separate triggers, not one combined trigger.

paraphrases: How does Exhaust work?
What does Exhaust mean?
Explain the Exhaust keyword.
explanation: Exhausting is an action that marks a non-spell Game Object on the board as "spent" — you show this by rotating the card 90 degrees. Once something is Exhausted, that's a state other rules and effects can check or reference. Most Exhaust actions come up as costs — a card's ability might read "Exhaust this" or "Exhaust me," shown by the Exhaust symbol, which represents paying that cost. An already-Exhausted object can't be Exhausted again.

paraphrases: How does Ready work?
What does the Ready state mean?
explanation: Readying is an action that marks a non-spell Game Object on the board as available for action — it's the opposite of Exhausted. Ready is a state other rules and card effects can check or reference, such as a spell that can only target Ready units.

paraphrases: How does Tank work?
What does the Tank keyword do?
Explain Tank.
explanation: Tank is a passive ability keyword. It's functionally short for "I must be assigned lethal damage before any other unit with the same controller as me that does not have Tank, during the Combat Damage step" — so during combat, a player has to finish assigning lethal damage to their Tank units before assigning it to non-Tank units. It only affects that combat-damage assignment order — it doesn't affect spell targeting. Multiple instances of Tank on the same unit are redundant; having it twice doesn't do anything extra.

paraphrases: How does Counter work?
What happens when a spell is countered?
Explain Countering.
explanation: Countering negates the execution, activation, or playing of a card or ability. A Countered card or ability does nothing at all and is cleared from the chain before it ever resolves — that includes not dealing damage or doing anything else its text says. It also isn't considered to have been played for abilities that trigger on cards being played, and countering never refunds the costs that were paid to play it.

paraphrases: How does Vision work?
What does the Vision keyword do?
Explain Vision.
explanation: Vision is a Triggered Ability keyword. If a unit has more than one instance of Vision, each one triggers separately rather than combining into a single trigger. Vision, and whether or not a permanent has it, is a characteristic other game effects can check.

paraphrases: How does Burn Out work?
What happens when I run out of cards in my deck?
explanation: Burning Out is what happens when you're required to move one or more cards from your Main Deck (most commonly, drawing) but there aren't enough cards left in it. When that happens: you perform as much of the action as you can, recycle your trash into your Main Deck (randomizing it), give an opponent 1 point, and then complete the rest of the original action. It isn't an instant loss — if your trash is also empty, you'll keep burning out and giving away points each time until an opponent reaches the win threshold.

paraphrases: If a unit with Vision is also Blinded, does Blinded cancel out Vision's effect?
Does the Blinded status stop a unit's Vision keyword from working?
explanation: I don't have rules evidence that establishes this — "Blinded" isn't a status or mechanic that appears anywhere in Riftbound's rules. I can tell you Vision is a real keyword, but I can't say how it would interact with something that isn't defined in this game, so I'm not going to guess.

paraphrases: Can a Frozen unit still attack?
Does Frozen stop a unit from being exhausted?
explanation: I don't have rules evidence that establishes this — "Frozen" isn't a status that appears anywhere in Riftbound's rules, so I can't say how it would interact with anything else in the game. I'm not going to guess at a mechanic that isn't defined.

paraphrases: If my unit is Poisoned, does it take damage every turn?
How does the Poison status work in Riftbound?
explanation: I don't have rules evidence that establishes this — "Poison"/"Poisoned" isn't a status that appears anywhere in Riftbound's rules. I can't describe how it would work when it isn't actually a mechanic in this game.

Can a Corrupted unit still be targeted by spells?

paraphrases: Can triggered abilities trigger on an opponent's turn without Reaction?
explanation:
Yes.
Whenever their condition is met, triggered abilities are added to the chain as pending items, regardless of whose turn it is. Rule 383.3 Rule 383.3.c

The Reaction keyword is not required for this to work on an opponent's turn.
Unlike spells and activated abilities which require Reaction to be played outside your turn, satisfying a trigger condition automatically creates the pending ability.
That ability must still finalize: it may be removed if its controller declines an initial "you may," if legal choices are unavailable, or if a required trigger cost is not paid. Rule 383.3.a.2 Rule 402.4 Rule 404.2

 Blade Dancer triggers when you choose a friendly unit.
 This can happen on your opponent's turn, for example when you play a Reaction spell that targets one of your own units.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I react to triggered and activated abilities?
explanation:
Yes, with one important exception: abilities that use the Add keyword.

All triggered and activated abilities are placed on the chain. Rule 377.3 Rule 383.3
However, abilities that add resources resolve immediately when finalized, which means players do not receive priority to react to them. Rule 337.2 Rule 429.2 Rule 429.2.a

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When do I choose whether to use a triggered ability that says "you may"?
explanation:
It depends on where "you may" appears in the ability's effect.

If "you may" is the first part of the effect, you decide whether to perform the ability during finalization. Rule 383.3.a Rule 402.1
If you decline, the pending ability is removed from the chain and considered not to have triggered. Rule 383.3.a.2 Rule 402.1.a
If you accept, you make all choices required for finalization and pay any costs incurred during finalization before the ability can finalize. Rule 402.2 Rule 404

If "you may" appears later in the effect, you decide whether to perform that instruction when the ability resolves. Rule 383.3.a.3

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When do I pay a cost in a triggered ability that says "you may"?
explanation:
It depends on where the cost appears in the triggered ability's effect.

In rules text phrased as "[do X] to [do Y]," the [do X] part is considered a cost within instructions.
If that cost appears at the beginning of a triggered effect or immediately after an initial "you may," it becomes the ability's base cost and must be paid during finalization. Rule 383.3.b Rule 383.3.b.1 Rule 740.4.a.2 Rule 403.1.b.1
If you decline to pay, the pending ability is removed from the chain without finalizing. Rule 404.2

If the cost appears later in the triggered effect, you pay it when the ability resolves. Rule 740.4.a.2.a

 Vayne, Hunter's ability reads "When I conquer, you may pay <Energy value={1} /> to return me to my owner's hand."
 It will trigger when you conquer.
 At finalization, you must decide whether to pay the <Energy value={1} /> cost.
 If you decline, the pending ability is removed from the chain.
 If you pay, the ability finalizes and opponents have the opportunity to react before it resolves.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I react to units being played?
explanation:
No, as units enter the board immediately without priority being passed to other players.

Unlike spells, units resolve the moment they are finalized and do not open a window of opportunity for reactions. Rule 337.2 Rule 359.2

If the unit has a play effect ("When you play me…"), or if another permanent's triggered ability fires as it enters the board, those triggered abilities are placed on the chain as pending items *after* the unit has already entered. Rule 383.4.a.2 Rule 383.2.c Rule 383.3
Once those pending items are finalized with no further items pending, priority passes and players may react Rule 337.4 — but by that point, the unit is already in play.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: In what order are multiple pending chain items finalized and resolved?
explanation:
Pending items are finalized in the order they were added, starting with the oldest. Rule 337.1 Rule 337.1.b
A unit, gear, or ability that adds resources resolves immediately when it finalizes. Rule 337.2
Other finalized items remain on the chain while the remaining pending items are processed.

Players do not receive priority until no pending items remain. Rule 337.3 Rule 337.4
After players pass priority, finalized chain items resolve in the opposite direction, starting with the newest. Rule 340.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I play a reaction after one, but not all, items on the chain have resolved?
explanation:
Yes, once you have gained priority.
The chain does not have to resolve in its entirety prior to (re)gaining priority, unlike in some other TCGs.

Any time the most recent item on the chain resolves and there are no pending items, the controller of the newest item on the chain gains priority. Rule 340.4

 You put Singularity on the chain targeting an opponent's unit.
 Your opponent reacts by putting their Wind Wall on the chain, attempting to counter the Singularity.
 In response, you play Stupefy, in the hopes of drawing into a counterspell of your own.
 Once Stupefy resolves and you draw a card, priority is back to your opponent as the most recent item is their Wind Wall.
 After they pass priority, you can react once again and play your own counterspell, assuming you drew it off of the Stupefy.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Outside a showdown, do I lose control of a battlefield as soon as my last unit leaves it?
explanation:
No, not immediately.

Outside a showdown, control of an empty battlefield is checked during a cleanup, not at the moment the last unit leaves.
You lose control only if the battlefield is still empty and the turn is in an open state. Rule 190.4.c Rule 323.6

If the chain still contains an item when a cleanup occurs, the turn is in a closed state and you keep control through that cleanup. Rule 309.1
You can lose control during a later cleanup after the turn returns to an open state if the battlefield remains empty.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: How is a card's total cost determined?
explanation:
A card's total cost is determined in a fixed sequence, rather than by applying every change at once:

1. Start with the card's base cost and apply any changes to it. Rule 356.1
2. Add all mandatory additional costs and any optional additional costs you chose to pay. Rule 356.2
3. Apply cost increases. Rule 356.3
4. Apply discounts. Rule 356.4
5. Apply any effects that modify the final total cost. Rule 356.5

Discounts that apply to one specific part of a cost are applied before discounts that apply to the total cost. Rule 356.4.c Rule 356.4.d
If multiple discounts apply within either group, you may choose their order. Rule 356.4.c.1 Rule 356.4.d.1
Any minimum imposed by a discount applies only to that discount, so a later discount can reduce the cost further. Rule 356.4.e

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Are paid costs refunded if a card or ability is countered?
explanation:
No.
Countering does not refund any costs paid to play a card, activate an ability, or trigger an ability, including additional costs. Rule 425.1.c Rule 425.1.c.1

A countered card or ability does nothing and is cleared from the chain, Rule 425.1.a but anything already spent, discarded, killed, or otherwise paid as a cost remains paid.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What are optional additional costs?
explanation:
Optional additional costs are additional costs a player may choose to pay. Rule 356.2.b.1

Their rules text uses both "may" and the exact phrase "as an additional cost."
Accelerate and Repeat are keyworded optional additional costs. Rule 805.1.a Rule 820.1.d

The player chooses whether to pay an optional additional cost while making relevant choices.
If chosen, it is included while determining the card's total cost before applicable discounts are applied. Rule 355.1.a Rule 356.2 Rule 356.4

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What costs still apply when I play a card ignoring one or more of its costs?
explanation:
Additional costs and cost increases still apply.
Playing a card "ignoring its cost" sets only its base energy and power costs to zero, while ignoring only its energy or power cost sets only that base cost to zero. Rule 356.1.b.1 Rule 356.1.b.2
Additional costs and cost increases are applied afterward and can raise its total cost above zero. Rule 356.1.b.3

Mandatory additional costs must still be paid, while optional additional costs may still be chosen and paid. Rule 356.2.a.1 Rule 356.2.b.1
By contrast, "ignoring any and all costs" sets the card's total cost to zero, including non-standard costs. Rule 356.5.a

Fizz, Trickster sets the chosen spell's base energy cost to <Energy value={0} />.
If an opponent controls Helm of Suppression, Helm's cost increase is applied afterward, so the spell costs <Energy value={1} />, or <Energy value={1} />Universal if Helm is Empowered. Rule 356.1.b.2 Rule 356.1.b.3 Rule 356.3

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can players react while costs are being paid?
explanation:
Not through a normal reaction window.
Costs are paid while the card or ability is being finalized, and finalization does not pass priority. Rule 357 Rule 404 Rule 337.1.a

When resources are required, the player paying them may activate eligible Add abilities with Reaction during that payment. Rule 429.3 Rule 444.2.c
This is a special permission for resource payment, not a normal reaction window: those abilities finalize and resolve immediately without passing priority. Rule 429.2 Rule 429.2.a

Any normal opportunity to react comes only after finalization, when the costs have already been paid.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a unit move when it enters the board?
explanation:
No.

Moving means changing a permanent's position from one space on the board to another. Rule 446.1
A card entering the board from another game zone is a zone change, not a move. Rule 446.2

Playing or creating a unit at a battlefield therefore does not fulfill an ability that triggers when the unit moves there.
Replacing where a unit enters the board also does not turn that entry into a move.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I choose a unit's current location as its move destination?
explanation:
No.

When an effect requires a player to choose a move destination for a unit, that destination must differ from the unit's current location. Rule 355.4 Rule 355.4.a
If the card specifies the destination instead, the player makes no destination choice and this restriction does not affect whether the unit is a legal target.
If the unit is already at that specified destination when the instruction resolves, the move is impossible and is ignored. Rule 055

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When does a card leave my trash when I play it from there?
explanation:
As soon as you begin playing it.
The first step of playing a card moves it from its current zone to the chain, where it waits to be finalized. Rule 354 Rule 354.2

Once you begin playing a card from your trash, it is no longer there while you make choices, determine its total cost, or resolve it.
If the card counts copies of itself in your trash, only the other copies still there count.
Likewise, if its cost is reduced for each card in your trash, it does not count itself toward that reduction.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When does a showdown close?
explanation:
Under normal game procedure, a showdown does not close abruptly.
It ends once all players have consecutively passed focus on an empty chain. Rule 348

 You control a battlefield with a 2 might Stalwart Poro on it.
 Your opponent moves their Ravenbloom Student into that battlefield starting a showdown.
 When combat opens, Stalwart Poro becomes a defender and its Shield increases its might to 3.
 Once your opponent gains focus, they play Hextech Ray targeting Stalwart Poro.
 Hextech Ray resolves, marking 3 damage on it.
 During the resulting cleanup, Stalwart Poro is killed for lethal damage. Rule 323.5
 The showdown *does not* end right away and you gain focus as usual.
 You still have the opportunity to play a legally timed card or ability in an attempt to prevent your opponent from conquering. Rule 347.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if another player's unit moves into an existing non-combat showdown?
explanation:
When a unit controlled by a different player becomes present during a non-combat showdown, combat is staged and the showdown becomes a combat showdown during the cleanup following that unit's arrival. Rule 316.8.b.1.a Rule 323.9 Rule 323.14

As combat opens, the player who originally applied contested status to the battlefield becomes the attacker, Rule 464.2.c.1 and the player who moves in during the showdown becomes the defender. Rule 464.2.c.2
Their units at that battlefield receive the corresponding designations then, Rule 464.2.c.3 enabling combat-related keywords such as Assault and Shield and causing attack or defend triggers to happen.

This interaction is commonly called the surprise defender: the player who first contested the battlefield remains the attacker, while the player joining later becomes the defender.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does "Kill a unit if it has 3 might or less" mean I can only choose a unit with 3 might or less?
explanation:
No.
Only words that describe the target restrict which objects can be chosen.

For example, "Kill a unit with 3 might or less" can target only a unit meeting that description. Rule 355.9.b

A separate condition on an effect does not restrict its targets.
"Kill a unit if it has 3 might or less" can target any otherwise legal unit; the might condition is checked when that instruction resolves.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if a target becomes illegal before a spell or ability resolves?
explanation:
The illegal target is unaffected, but the spell or ability still resolves.
Instructions related to that target cannot be followed, while independent instructions continue normally. Rule 359.3.e.5 Rule 359.3.e.6

If an instruction needs information from the illegal target, that information is null and calculations using it are ignored. Rule 359.3.e.12
If a later instruction is linked to an earlier instruction that was ignored, the later instruction is also ignored. Rule 359.3.e.14.a

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I use Ambush to play a unit to my base?
explanation:
No.
Ambush only permits playing a unit to a battlefield; it has no effect on your base.

Ambush is shorthand for "I may be played to a battlefield where you control units" and "I have Reaction as long as I'm being played to a battlefield where you control units." Rule 822.1.b
The permission Ambush grants is strictly limited to battlefields — a base is not a battlefield, so Ambush never makes it a valid destination. Rule 822.1.c
Playing a unit to your base is already permitted by the default rules for valid locations, Rule 355.2.a but choosing base does not grant the unit Reaction.
It can be played there only at its normal timing.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can opponents react to a unit being played with Ambush?
explanation:
No.
Ambush grants the unit Reaction speed, which determines when it can be played — it does not create a window for opponents to respond before the unit enters.

Units resolve the moment they are finalized without entering the Execute step, Rule 337.2 and finalization does not pass priority. Rule 337.1.a
The unit enters the board immediately, just as any unit played during an open state would (see also Can I react to units being played?).

This is a common point of confusion with cards like Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror, which has Ambush and triggers if an enemy unit is alone when he attacks or defends.
An opponent cannot play a unit in response to Kha'Zix being placed on the chain in an attempt to break the "alone" condition before he enters.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Who gets to act after I Ambush a unit during a showdown?
explanation:
It depends on whether anything else remains on the chain once the unit enters.

When played onto an empty chain, the unit enters immediately, the chain empties, and the turn returns to an open state during the showdown — focus passes to the next player in turn order. Rule 340.2.a
This catches many players off guard — you move in to attack, Ambush a unit, and expect to retain focus, but your opponent gets to act first.

When played in response to something already on the chain — such as attack or defend triggers, or a spell — the turn does not return to an open state after the unit resolves, so focus does not pass. Rule 346
Priority instead passes to the controller of the newest remaining item on the chain. Rule 340.4

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When is a Deathknell ability added to the chain?
explanation:
A Deathknell ability is added to the chain as a pending item before the dying permanent moves to the trash. Rule 808.1.d.2
Before the permanent leaves the board, the game records its location, attributes, and other information needed by its ability. Rule 808.1.d.3
If the permanent's death is replaced and it is not sent to the trash, the pending ability is removed from the chain. Rule 808.1.d.1
Each instance of Deathknell triggers separately and creates its own pending item. Rule 808.2 Rule 808.2.a

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When does a Deathknell ability resolve if its unit dies during a cleanup?
explanation:
After the cleanup finishes.
The ability becomes a pending item before the unit moves to the trash. Rule 323.4 Rule 323.5 Rule 808.1.d.2
The remaining cleanup steps are then completed before that pending ability can be finalized. Rule 334

During a combat cleanup, this means surviving units are healed before the Deathknell ability is finalized or resolved. Rule 466.1.a.1
After the cleanup, the ability is finalized, any required targets are chosen, and players receive priority before it resolves. Rule 334.2 Rule 337.4

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Deathknell resolve before the card or ability that killed the unit?
explanation:
It depends on when the unit is killed and what kind of chain item caused it.

Killed as a cost:
If a unit is killed to pay a cost, the kill happens while the card or ability is being finalized. Rule 357.2 Rule 404.1
The Deathknell ability becomes pending above that chain item. Rule 808.1.d.2

If the original item is a spell or an ability that does not add resources, the pending Deathknell ability is finalized before play continues. Rule 359.3.b Rule 406.3
Because it is newer on the chain, the Deathknell ability resolves before that spell or ability. Rule 340.1

If the original item is a unit, gear, or ability that adds resources, it resolves immediately when finalized, before the pending Deathknell ability is processed. Rule 337.2
The Deathknell ability resolves afterward.

Killed during resolution:
If a resolving card or ability kills the unit, that chain item continues resolving without interruption. Rule 354.3
The Deathknell ability becomes pending, but it cannot be finalized until the current chain item finishes resolving. Rule 334.2
The killing card or ability therefore finishes before the Deathknell ability can resolve.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can opponents react to an Empower ability?
explanation:
Yes.
Empower is an activated ability keyword, Rule 827.1 and activated abilities use the chain. Rule 377.3
After the ability is finalized, opponents have an opportunity to react before it resolves. Rule 377.3.b.2

This differs from activated abilities that use Add, which resolve immediately when finalized and cannot be reacted to. Rule 337.2 Rule 429.2
See also Can I react to triggered and activated abilities?.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When can I activate an Empower ability?
explanation:
By default, only during your own Main Phase while the turn is in a neutral open state.

An Empower ability is an activated ability, Rule 827.1 and activated abilities can normally be activated only on their controller's turn during an open state. Rule 381
Because Empower has neither Action nor Reaction by default, it cannot be activated during a showdown or in response to another chain item. Rule 308.1.a Rule 309.1.a

An Empower ability may have text that changes its timing. Rule 827.1.c.4
If it explicitly has Action or Reaction, follow the permissions of that keyword instead.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a "When I become Empowered" ability trigger if the unit leaves the board before its Empower ability resolves?
explanation:
No.
If the unit is killed, returned to hand, or otherwise leaves the board before its Empower ability resolves, it does not become Empowered and its "When I become Empowered" ability does not trigger.

The Empower ability remains on the chain, but the Empowered state exists only for game objects on the board. Rule 441.2
Because triggered abilities of permanents can evaluate their conditions only while their source is on the board, its dependent "When I become Empowered" ability is not active and does not trigger. Rule 384.2 Rule 828.1.c Rule 828.1.d

 A player activates Mel, Defiant Soul's Empower ability by discarding a spell.
 An opponent responds with Star-Crossed and returns Mel to her owner's hand.
 When the Empower ability resolves, Mel is no longer a game object on the board and does not become Empowered.
 Her "When I become Empowered" ability does not trigger, so no enemy unit is banished.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can a unit or gear without an Empower or Empowered ability become Empowered?
explanation:
Yes, if a game effect instructs a player to empower it.

The Empowered state can apply to game objects on the board; it is not restricted to cards with printed Empower or Empowered abilities. Rule 441.1 Rule 441.2
Players cannot empower a game object at will, however; they may do so only when directed by a game effect. Rule 441.3 Rule 441.3.a

 Sanction can empower any unit that is a legal choice, even if that unit has no printed reference to Empower or Empowered.
 Once that unit is Empowered, effects such as Aurok General's ability can identify and affect it normally.

 Hextech Formula can empower another gear, even if that gear has no printed reference to Empower or Empowered.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens to attached equipment when a unit dies?
explanation:
The equipment detaches and remains at the unit's last location, recalling if at a battlefield.

When a unit with attached equipment dies, the equipment detaches and remains at the location the unit occupied before dying. Rule 719.5 Rule 435.4.b

If that location is a battlefield, the detached equipment will be recalled to its controller's base during the next cleanup. Rule 435.4.a
If that location is the controller's base, the equipment simply remains there.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens to attached equipment when you take control of an enemy unit?
explanation:
Equipment stays attached but its controller does not change — only the top-most unit's controller changes.

When you take control of a unit, any equipment attached to it retains its current controller.
Changes in control of the top-most card do not affect control of attached cards, and vice versa. Rule 718.5.f

When the equipment detaches, it remains at the unit's last location. Rule 719.5 Rule 435.4.b
If that location is a battlefield, it is recalled to its controller's base during the next cleanup. Rule 435.4.a
If that location is another player's base, the equipment remains there until the next cleanup, when it is recalled to its controller's base. Rule 323.7

Because the equipment remains under the other player's control, that player can play a unit with Weaponmaster and choose the equipment, even while it is attached to the unit you control. Rule 718.5.b Rule 821.1.c
If its Equip cost can be paid and it can legally be detached and attached, it moves to the newly played unit. Rule 821.1.c.4 Rule 821.1.c.5

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Do Equip, Quick-Draw, or Weaponmaster count as choosing a unit?
explanation:
Equip and QuickDraw choose units; Weaponmaster does not.

Some abilities trigger or care about when you choose friendly units.
Here's how equipment-related effects interact with such abilities:

- When you activate a gear's Equip ability, you choose a unit you control to attach the equipment to. Rule 818.1.b.1
This choice is a target, so activating Equip counts as choosing a unit. Rule 355.7
- When you play a gear with QuickDraw, its triggered ability instructs you to "attach it to a Unit you control". Rule 819.1.d
While attaching cards doesn't inherently choose or specify a target, Rule 434.3 QuickDraw's ability does require you to choose which unit to attach to. Rule 355.10
This counts as choosing a unit.
- When you play a unit with Weaponmaster, you choose an equipment you control, not the unit. Rule 821.1.c
The rules explicitly state that "The Equip ability is not activated this way, and the unit with the Weaponmaster ability is not chosen". Rule 821.1.c.6
Therefore, Weaponmaster does not count as choosing a unit.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can opponents react to Equip, Quick-Draw, or Weaponmaster abilities?
explanation:
Yes — all three equipment-related abilities create chain items that opponents can respond to before the attachment resolves.

Equip is an activated ability. Rule 818.1
Activated abilities use the chain, Rule 377.3 so when you activate Equip, opponents have an opportunity to play a Reaction spell or ability before the attachment resolves. Rule 377.3.b.2

When you play a QuickDraw gear, the gear itself resolves immediately when finalized and cannot be reacted to. Rule 337.2
However, QuickDraw's triggered ability — "When you play this, attach it to a unit you control" Rule 819.1.d — is placed on the chain as a separate item. Rule 383.4.a.2
Opponents can respond to that ability before the attachment resolves.

Weaponmaster is also a triggered ability keyword. Rule 821.1
Its ability triggers when you play the unit, and is placed on the chain just like any other triggered ability. Rule 383.4.a.2
Opponents can respond to it before the equipment is attached.

Skipping straight to attaching without checking for reactions is not correct play for any of these abilities.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When can I play a spell using Flow?
explanation:
You can play it only when its existing timing restrictions allow.

Flow lets you play the spell from your trash for its Flow cost, but it changes no other permissions or timing restrictions. Rule 829.1.b Rule 829.1.b.2
For example, Flow does not grant a spell Reaction or let you play an Action outside its normal timing.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Where does a spell played using Flow go if it is countered?
explanation:
It is banished unless another replacement effect changes that result.

Countering clears the spell from the chain and would normally put it in the trash. Rule 425.1.a Rule 425.1.a.1
However, playing a spell using Flow creates a delayed replacement effect that banishes it if it would leave the chain after becoming finalized, unless its own execution instructed it to leave. Rule 829.1.b.1
Being countered meets those conditions, so the Flow replacement effect banishes the spell instead of letting it go to the trash.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Defy counter a spell whose Flow cost exceeds Defy's limit?
explanation:
Yes, provided the spell's printed cost meets Defy's restrictions.

Defy checks the cost of its target, and effects that determine a card's cost always use its printed or copied cost rather than the amount actually paid. Rule 206
A Flow cost is an alternate cost that replaces the spell's base cost during finalization, Rule 829.1.c.1 but it does not change the printed cost that Defy checks.

 Lacerate has a printed cost of <Energy value={2} />Order and a Flow cost of <Energy value={4} />OrderOrder.
 Defy can counter it because Defy checks the printed cost, not the Flow cost paid.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Where does a Flow spell countered by Abandon go?
explanation:
It is banished rather than returned to its owner's hand.

Abandon replaces putting the countered spell in the trash with returning it to its owner's hand, while Flow replaces the spell leaving the chain with banishing it. Rule 425.1.a.1 Rule 829.1.b.1
Because both replacement effects apply to the affected spell's departure from the chain, that spell's controller chooses their order. Rule 372

The result is the same in either order.
If Flow applies first, the spell is banished instead of going to the trash, so Abandon no longer has a qualifying event to replace.
If Abandon applies first, it still replaces the original event with the spell leaving the chain for its owner's hand, so Flow applies to that replacement event and banishes the spell instead. Rule 370.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What does Repeat repeat?
explanation:
Repeat executes a spell or ability's instructions an additional time during resolution; it does not create another copy or chain item. Rule 820.1.d.1 Rule 820.3.a
The spell or ability is played only once, so its costs are paid only once during its original finalization.

Targets, modes, and other choices are made separately for each execution. Rule 820.2 Rule 820.2.a
Those choices may differ between the original and additional executions.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if a spell with Repeat is countered?
explanation:
The entire spell is countered, including all repeated instructions.

Repeat does *not* create a second instance of the spell on the chain. Rule 820.3.a
Instead, it modifies how the spell resolves by executing its instructions an additional time. Rule 820.1.d.1

When a spell is countered, it does nothing and is cleared from the chain. Rule 425.1.a
Since the spell never resolves, none of its instructions are executed, whether they came from Repeat or not.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Abandoned Hall's ability trigger if the spell is countered?
explanation:
No.
Abandoned Hall's ability triggers "when a player plays a spell," and a countered spell is not considered played.

A card is only played once the entire play process has finished in its entirety. Rule 350.1
Abilities that trigger on playing a card fire when that act has been completed by the card's resolution; Rule 419.4.a if a game effect prevents resolution — for example because the spell was countered — the card is not considered to have been played and no abilities that trigger on playing cards fire. Rule 419.4.a.1
This follows directly from what countering does: a countered card is cleared from the chain and is not considered to have been played. Rule 425.1.b

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can a unit moved into or away from Abandoned Hall by a spell be chosen?
explanation:
Only if it is at Abandoned Hall after the spell fully resolves.

A card is only considered "played" once the entire play process has finished, Rule 350.1 which for spells means after all instructions have been executed and the card is placed in the trash.
Abandoned Hall's triggered ability therefore fires after the spell resolves, not when it is placed on the chain. Rule 419.4.a Rule 383.2.c
By then, a unit moved into Abandoned Hall is present and can be chosen, while a unit moved away no longer qualifies as "a unit they control here."

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: How are targets chosen when playing Alpha Strike?
explanation:
When finalizing Alpha Strike on the chain, choose the friendly unit, then choose up to one enemy unit at a battlefield per point of its current might.

The friendly unit is chosen explicitly as a standard target.
The enemy units are targets generated by the split-target instruction. Rule 355.14.a Rule 355.14.b Rule 355.14.c
You may choose fewer enemy units than the friendly unit's current might, including zero. Rule 355.14.c

Since each chosen enemy unit is a target of Alpha Strike, Deflect is added as a mandatory additional cost for any of those units that have it during finalization. Rule 356.2.a.2 Rule 809.1.d

All choices are locked in at finalization and cannot be changed after this step. Rule 355.15

 You play Alpha Strike and choose a friendly unit with 4 might.
 You may then choose up to 4 enemy units at battlefields as the split targets.
 You choose 3.
 Those 3 units — and the friendly unit — are all locked in as targets.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When is Alpha Strike's damage distribution decided?
explanation:
The distribution of damage across the chosen enemy units is decided at resolution, not at finalization. Rule 355.14.e

The total damage available equals the friendly unit's effective might when Alpha Strike resolves — meaning any Reaction speed buffs or debuffs applied by either player between finalization and resolution will affect the damage pool. Rule 359.3.f.2

Each chosen target must receive at least 1 damage. Rule 355.14.f Rule 355.14.g
Beyond that minimum, you may distribute the remaining damage among those targets however you choose, but all available damage must be distributed.

 You chose 3 enemy units at finalization.
 When Alpha Strike resolves, your friendly unit has 6 might.
 You must assign at least 1 damage to each of the 3 targets.
 The remaining 3 damage can go wherever you choose — 4/1/1, 2/2/2, 1/1/4, and so on.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What if the chosen friendly unit leaves the board or becomes illegal before Alpha Strike resolves?
explanation:
It remains legal if it only moves to another board location while remaining a friendly unit; otherwise, Alpha Strike deals no damage.

Alpha Strike does not require the chosen friendly unit to be at a particular location.
If it moves elsewhere on the board but remains a friendly unit, it is still a legal target and deals damage using its effective might when Alpha Strike resolves. Rule 359.3.e.2 Rule 359.3.f.2

If the target changes to a non-board zone, stops being a unit, or stops being friendly, it is illegal as Alpha Strike resolves. Rule 359.3.e.2
Alpha Strike still resolves, but the illegal target is unaffected and the "its Might" referent returns null, so the related damage instruction is ignored. Rule 359.3.e.5 Rule 359.3.e.12 Rule 359.3.f.2.a

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What if a chosen enemy unit leaves a battlefield or becomes illegal before Alpha Strike resolves?
explanation:
It receives no damage from Alpha Strike.

Each chosen enemy unit must still be an enemy unit at a battlefield when Alpha Strike resolves.
If one moves to base or otherwise stops meeting those requirements, it is an illegal target and is unaffected by the spell. Rule 359.3.e.2 Rule 359.3.e.5

Alpha Strike still distributes its damage among any remaining legal enemy targets. Rule 359.3.e.8
If every chosen enemy unit is illegal, the damage instruction does not execute. Rule 359.3.e.7

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Applied Researchers reduce Repeat, Flow, and Deflect costs?
explanation:
Yes, provided Applied Researchers is Empowered and the cost belongs to a spell.

Repeat is an optional additional cost. Rule 820.1 Rule 820.1.c.1
Deflect imposes a mandatory additional cost on a spell or ability that targets the permanent with Deflect. Rule 356.2.a.2 Rule 809.1.d
Discounts can reduce both kinds of additional costs, including to zero. Rule 356.4.f

A Flow cost is an alternate cost that replaces a spell's base cost during finalization. Rule 829.1.c.1
Applied Researchers' discount is applied afterward when determining the spell's total cost. Rule 356.1 Rule 356.4

Applied Researchers can therefore reduce a Repeat or Deflect cost paid while playing a spell.
It cannot reduce either cost when playing an ability, because its discount applies only to spells. Rule 820.1.a Rule 809.1.d

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Applied Researchers reduce Shock Blast's cost to zero?
explanation:
Yes, if Applied Researchers is Empowered, you can play Shock Blast for <Energy value={0} />.
Applied Researchers itself satisfies Shock Blast's requirement that you control something that is Empowered, so both cards' discounts apply.

Both abilities discount Shock Blast's total cost during the Determine Total Cost step of playing it. Rule 356.4
Discounts that apply to the total cost may be applied in any order, Rule 356.4.d Rule 356.4.d.1 and a minimum imposed by one discount applies only to that discount. Rule 356.4.e

Cost Determination Sequence:
1. Shock Blast starts with its base cost of <Energy value={3} />Mind.
2. Apply Researchers' discount first, reducing that cost by <Energy value={1} />Universal to <Energy value={2} />.
This satisfies Researchers' minimum of <Energy value={1} />.
3. Apply Shock Blast's own discount next, reducing its remaining energy cost by <Energy value={2} /> to <Energy value={0} />.

Applying the discounts in the opposite order would leave the spell costing <Energy value={1} />, but you may choose the order that results in the lower cost.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When exactly does Astral Heron trigger, and which card gets its discount?
explanation:
Astral Heron triggers after your first card of the turn finishes resolving, not when that card is placed on the chain or finalized.
In a trigger condition, "When you play" is checked only when the act of playing that card is completed by its resolution. Rule 350.1 Rule 419.4.a
If a spell is countered instead of resolving, it does not trigger Astral Heron, and the first card you later resolve that turn can trigger it instead. Rule 419.4.a.1

The triggered ability is then placed on the chain and must resolve before the discount exists. Rule 383.3 Rule 390.4
Once it resolves, "your next card" means the next card you place on the chain and queue for finalization. Rule 419.1
Astral Heron's discount is applied while determining that card's total cost, before you pay the cost and finish finalizing it. Rule 356.4 Rule 357

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Astral Heron's ability trigger if it's your first card played to a battlefield this turn?
explanation:
Yes — assuming it's played to a battlefield.

Play, in a trigger condition, refers to a card resolving, not merely being placed on the chain. Rule 350.1 Rule 419.4.a
Units resolve immediately after they finalize. Rule 337.2
During that resolution, the unit becomes a game object, its passive abilities become active, and it enters the board at its chosen location. Rule 359.2 Rule 359.2.a Rule 359.2.c

A trigger's condition is evaluated after a potentially inciting event has been processed, and nothing requires that event to have been caused by a *different* card. Rule 383.2.c Rule 383.2.c.1
"When you play your first card each turn" begins the trigger condition, Rule 383.2.a and "if I'm at a battlefield" immediately follows it, so that additional requirement is also part of the trigger condition and is checked when the condition is fulfilled. Rule 383.2.a.1
After Astral Heron finishes resolving, play-trigger conditions are evaluated. Rule 419.4.a
If it's the first card played this turn, Astral Heron is already at the battlefield when its condition is checked, so its ability is placed on the chain.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Astral Heron trigger if your first card moves it to base?
explanation:
No.
If a spell such as Flash or Emperor's Divide moves Astral Heron to base while resolving, Astral Heron is no longer at a battlefield when its trigger condition is checked.

A card is not considered played, and abilities that trigger from playing it are not evaluated, until that card finishes resolving. Rule 350.1 Rule 419.4.a
Astral Heron's trigger condition is therefore checked only after the spell's movement instructions have been completed. Rule 383.2.c
Because "if I'm at a battlefield" is part of that trigger condition, the ability is not placed on the chain if Astral Heron is at base by then. Rule 383.2.a.1

This differs from moving Astral Heron after its triggered ability has already been placed on the chain.
At that point, the condition has already been satisfied.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Once Astral Heron's triggered ability is on the chain, can killing or moving it stop the cost reduction?
explanation:
No.
Once the triggered ability is on the chain, killing or moving Astral Heron does not stop the discount from applying to your next card.

"If I'm at a battlefield" is part of the trigger condition, so it's only checked when the triggering event occurs to decide whether the ability is placed on the chain — it is not re-checked when the ability later resolves. Rule 383.2.a.1
Nothing in the effect references Astral Heron's location or continued presence, so removing it does not stop the trigger from creating the discount.
Once created, that discount is a delayed ability and executes at its specified time regardless of whether Astral Heron remains on the board. Rule 392

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Azir, Sovereign is killed or returned to his base before his attack trigger resolves, do token units still move?
explanation:
No.
"This battlefield" is a referent: information drawn from the source of the ability itself. Rule 359.3.f.1
Referents are checked at the moment the instruction executes, not when the trigger was placed on the chain. Rule 359.3.f.2

If Azir has been moved to his base or killed before the trigger resolves, there is no "this battlefield" to move token units to.
The instruction cannot be followed and is ignored. Rule 359.3.e.6

"This battlefield" is not a target.
It is programmatically determined from Azir's current location, since he can only ever be at one battlefield at a time — no choice is ever made. Rule 355.10.d Rule 355.10.d.1

Two common plays that produce this outcome:

- Hidden Blade, when played from its facedown zone, can be used in response to Azir's attack trigger to kill him at Reaction speed.
- Overzealous Fan's defend trigger fires simultaneously with Azir's attack trigger when combat designations are assigned.
 Because Azir's controller places their trigger first, Overzealous Fan's trigger sits above it on the chain and resolves first, potentially moving Azir to his base before his own trigger resolves. Rule 464.2.e.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if the targeted unit is removed before Baited Hook's ability resolves?
explanation:
The unit can't be killed, and no unit can be banished from the top 5, since nothing can satisfy a might comparison against a null value.

If the friendly unit is no longer a legal target when the ability resolves — for example, if it was returned to its owner's hand in response — it is unaffected by the ability's "kill" instruction. Rule 359.3.e.2 Rule 359.3.e.5
Because the unit was never killed, any information the ability checks about it, including its might, returns null. Rule 359.3.e.12
"Banish a unit with might up to 1 more than the killed unit" can never be satisfied against a null might, so no unit can be chosen from among the top 5 cards, even though you still look at them.
"Then recycle the rest" is unaffected by this, since it isn't tied to the killed unit's might — you still recycle every card you looked at that wasn't banished.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Baited Hook kills Glasc Mixologist and plays Karthus, Eternal, does Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell trigger twice?
explanation:
No.
Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell has already triggered once by the time Karthus, Eternal enters the board.

When Baited Hook kills Glasc Mixologist, Glasc's Deathknell is added to the chain as a pending item before he is moved to the trash. Rule 428.1.a.1.b Rule 808.1.d.2
Baited Hook then continues resolving and may banish Karthus from among the top 5 cards and play him, placing him on the chain above Glasc's Deathknell. Rule 354.2

Karthus enters the board before Glasc's Deathknell resolves, but his passive ability is only active while he is on the board. Rule 365.1
It was not active when Glasc's Deathknell triggered, and by the time Karthus enters, that ability has already been finalized.
Karthus entering the board does not cause it to trigger again.
Glasc's Deathknell resolves once, so it can play only one unit from the trash.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Baron Nashor move to the Baron Pit when it's created as part of playing him?
explanation:
No.
Baron Nashor enters the Baron Pit directly — his entry location is replaced, not his position on the board.
A move is defined as a permanent changing position from one space on the board to another. Rule 446.1
Baron Nashor is entering the board for the first time (a zone change), which is not a move. Rule 446.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens after Baron Nashor enters the Baron Pit?
explanation:
A non-combat showdown opens during the resulting cleanup.

Resolution Sequence:
1. The Baron Pit is newly created and has no controller when Baron Nashor enters it. Rule 439.4.b
2. Baron Nashor entering the uncontrolled battlefield applies contested status to it. Rule 190.3.a.1
3. During the resulting cleanup, a non-combat showdown is marked as staged at the Baron Pit. Rule 316.8.b Rule 323.8
4. Later in that cleanup, the staged showdown opens. Rule 323.12 Rule 344.2

If an opposing unit arrives at the Baron Pit during the showdown, a combat is staged and the non-combat showdown becomes a combat showdown during the following cleanup. Rule 316.8.b.1.a Rule 323.9 Rule 323.14

If the showdown closes with only Baron Nashor's controller's units present at the Baron Pit, and they have not yet scored it this turn, they conquer it and score. Rule 348.2.a Rule 348.2.a.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does the Baron Pit need to be scored to win by conquering?
explanation:
Yes.
Winning by conquering at match point requires having scored every battlefield on the board that turn — including the Baron Pit. Rule 471.1.b.1
If it hasn't been scored, the winning conquer draws a card instead.

Winning by hold is unaffected, as it has no such requirement. Rule 471.1.a.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I play Baron Nashor while an opponent's Mageseeker Warden is at a battlefield?
explanation:
It depends on whether the Baron Pit is already on the board.

If the Baron Pit is not yet on the board, Baron Nashor enters the Baron Pit, not your base.
As Baron Nashor is played, his "as you play me" instruction fires during the playing process — the Baron Pit battlefield token is added to the board. Rule 135.2.b.3 Rule 187.9
Under Mageseeker Warden's restriction, your base is the only valid playing location — where Baron Nashor is nominally played to — but his replacement effect overrides where he actually enters. Rule 355.2.a
His "If you do, I enter there" then functions as a replacement effect that applies as he enters the board, replacing his entry at his original play location with entry at the Baron Pit. Rule 369.3 Rule 370.1.b

If the Baron Pit is already on the board, the "as you play me" instruction does nothing — the Baron Pit token is only added if it's not there already — so the "If you do" condition is not met.
Baron Nashor simply enters his base, the only valid playing location under Mageseeker Warden's restriction. Rule 355.2.a

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Bone Skewer choose a unit that says it "can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities"?
explanation:
Yes, as the untargetability is inactive in hand and hand cards cannot be targeted in any case.

Ruin Runner and Baron Nashor are made untargetable by passive abilities declaring that they can't be chosen by some category of spells and abilities. Rule 757 Rule 757.1
Passive abilities of permanents are typically active only while on the board. Rule 365.1
Abilities that function in another zone self-describe that context, Rule 366.1 which these untargetability abilities do not.
They therefore have no effect while the unit is in hand.
Beyond that, Bone Skewer never targets the chosen unit in the first place — cards in hand are never targets because the hand is not a public zone, Rule 355.10.a so there is no finalization step at which a unit there could be declared as a target. Rule 355.5

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Bone Skewer stun a unit that can't be chosen by enemy spells or abilities?
explanation:
Yes, because the reflexive trigger that stuns the unit does not ask its controller to choose anything.

If the opponent plays the unit, Bone Skewer's "then do this" wording creates a reflexive trigger as a pending item on the chain. Rule 387.1 Rule 387.2 Rule 388.1
The trigger is linked to the preceding ability, and "it" can only refer to the unit played by that ability. Rule 394.1 Rule 397
When the trigger is finalized, no choice is made about which unit will be stunned; it is always and only that unit.
Because the unit is programmatically determined rather than chosen, it is not a target. Rule 355.10.d Rule 355.10.d.1

This means untargetability — the "can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities" passive on units like Ruin Runner and Baron Nashor — does not prevent the stun, since it only stops a unit from being chosen as a target and the stun targets nothing. Rule 758
Deflect is similarly irrelevant, since Deflect is only added as a cost when a spell or ability chooses an opponent's permanent, Rule 809.1.d which is not the case here.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If a unit chosen by Bone Skewer has Hidden, can the opponent hide it instead of playing it?
explanation:
No, hiding the unit does not fulfill Bone Skewer's instruction to play it.

Hide is a separate action, not a subset of play. Rule 811.1.c.1
Even though the chosen unit is in hand and may have Hidden, Bone Skewer instructs the opponent to play it as a limited action. Rule 419.3
That play follows the normal process unless Bone Skewer says otherwise, Rule 419.3.b so the unit is put on the chain and queued for finalization. Rule 419.1
The opponent cannot choose to hide it instead.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Brynhir Thundersong stop cards already on the chain?
explanation:
No.
Once Brynhir Thundersong's play effect resolves, opponents cannot play further cards that turn, but cards already on the chain are unaffected.

To play a card means to place it on the chain and queue it for finalization. Rule 419.1
A pending card has already been placed on the chain and queued for finalization, Rule 329.1 Rule 354.2 and a finalized card has progressed beyond that point. Rule 329.3
Brynhir Thundersong therefore does not stop either from finalizing or resolving.

See also What does "play" mean on a card?.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I choose a unit's current battlefield as Call to Battle's destination?
explanation:
No, because Call to Battle requires the player to choose the move destination, so the restriction on valid destinations applies directly.

When a spell or ability has the player choose a move destination, that destination must be somewhere other than the unit's current location. Rule 355.4 Rule 355.4.a
Call to Battle has the player choose both the unit and the battlefield, so the chosen battlefield cannot be the unit's current location.
If no valid destination can be chosen for the selected unit, the spell cannot be finalized.

This contrasts with Flash, which specifies its destination — base — rather than requiring the player to choose one.
Because no destination choice is made when playing Flash, this restriction never applies, and a unit already in base is a valid target.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When I play Consuming Curse from my trash, does it count itself for the bonus damage?
explanation:
No.
Playing Consuming Curse from your trash moves it onto the chain first, Rule 354 Rule 419.1 so it's no longer in your trash to be counted.
Only the *other* copies still in your trash add bonus damage.

Shadow Assassin and Shadowblade Lurker work the same way.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Diana, Lunari's ability resolve before or after attack and defend abilities from the start of combat?
explanation:
Diana's ability resolves after all attack and defend triggers generated as that combat opens.

When combat opens with a combat showdown, the attacker and defender designations are assigned to units. Rule 464.2.c.3
Attack triggers fire when a unit gains the attacker designation, and defend triggers fire when a unit gains the defender designation. Rule 383.4.e Rule 383.4.f
Those triggers are then added to the combat chain, with the attacking player placing theirs first, followed by others in turn order, and the defending player last. Rule 464.2.e Rule 464.2.e.1

Diana's "when a showdown begins here" trigger is a start-of-showdown effect, which the combat-opening sequence processes as its very first step — before designations are established and their attack and defend triggers are added to the chain. Rule 464.2.b
Because the chain resolves newest-item-first, Diana's ability resolves last — after every attack and defend trigger from that same combat chain has already resolved. Rule 340.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: How long does Endless Riches make you skip your Draw Phase?
explanation:
You skip every Draw Phase you would have for as long as Endless Riches remains on the board.

"Skip your Draw Phase" is a passive ability and a replacement effect that replaces your Draw Phase with nothing. Rule 364.2 Rule 443.1.a
Passive abilities of permanents become active when the permanent enters the board and are typically active only while it remains there. Rule 359.2.a Rule 365.1
Once Endless Riches leaves the board, this ability is no longer active, so your later Draw Phases occur normally.

This is not a delayed ability that applies only to your next Draw Phase or only during a particular turn.
Delayed abilities specify the window during which they apply, Rule 390 but Endless Riches specifies no such window.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I hide cards from my trash while Endless Riches is on the board?
explanation:
No, Endless Riches does not allow you to hide cards from your trash.

Endless Riches grants permission only to play cards from your trash, and hiding a card is not a subset of playing it. Rule 811.1.c.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Where does a spell played by Fizz, Trickster or Kai'Sa, Evolutionary go while Endless Riches is in play?
explanation:
It is recycled.
The "then recycle it" text on Fizz, Trickster and Kai'Sa, Evolutionary creates a delayed replacement effect that replaces the spell leaving the chain with recycling it. Rule 390.3.a
Endless Riches also creates a replacement effect that would replace the spell going to the trash with banishing it.

The result is the same regardless of the order in which the spell's controller applies these replacement effects. Rule 372
If the delayed replacement is applied first, the spell is recycled instead of going to the trash, so Endless Riches no longer applies.
If Endless Riches is applied first, the spell would be banished instead of going to the trash, but it is still leaving the chain, so the delayed replacement replaces that event with recycling it. Rule 370.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Which costs does Ezreal reduce?
explanation:
Ezreal reduces only optional additional costs you choose to pay.
These costs use both the word "may" and the exact phrase "as an additional cost." Rule 356.2.b.1
Accelerate and Repeat are keyworded optional additional costs, so Ezreal reduces them too. Rule 805.1.a Rule 820.1.d

Ezreal's discount applies to the optional additional cost itself as soon as that cost is added, before discounts that apply to the card's total cost. Rule 356.4.c Rule 356.4.d

Mandatory additional costs are not optional because they omit "may," Rule 356.2.a.1 and payments made while carrying out an effect are not additional costs to play that card.
Ezreal does not reduce either kind of payment.

 Blast Corps Cadet says "You may pay <Energy value={1} />Fury as an additional cost to play me."
 Ezreal can reduce that optional additional cost to either <Energy value={1} /> or Fury.
 By contrast, Ezreal does not reduce Cruel Patron's mandatory cost to kill a friendly unit or the <Energy value={2} /> an opponent may pay during Hard Bargain's effect.
 Ezreal does reduce Hard Bargain's separate Repeat cost.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Fallen Feline stop a named spell already on the chain?
explanation:
No.
Fallen Feline prevents opponents from playing further spells with the chosen name while it is at a battlefield, but it does not affect spells already on the chain.

To play a card means to place it on the chain and queue it for finalization. Rule 419.1
A pending spell has already been placed on the chain and queued for finalization, Rule 329.1 Rule 354.2 and a finalized spell has progressed beyond that point. Rule 329.3
Fallen Feline therefore does not stop either from finalizing or resolving.

See also What does "play" mean on a card?.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Flash target a unit that is already in base?
explanation:
Yes, because Flash specifies its destination rather than requiring the player to choose one.

When a spell or ability has the player choose a move destination, that destination must be somewhere other than the unit's current location. Rule 355.4 Rule 355.4.a
Flash, however, does not ask the player to choose a destination: the card specifies it as base.
That step of the play process never occurs, so this restriction never applies.

The only choice the player makes when playing Flash is which friendly units to target. Rule 355.5
A unit in base is a friendly unit and meets no other targeting restriction, so it is a valid target. Rule 355.9.b

When Flash resolves and instructs the game to move that unit to base, the instruction is impossible — a unit cannot move to its current location.
Impossible instructions are ignored, and everything else resolves normally. Rule 055

Azir, Ascendant illustrates the same principle: its ability says "Move me to its location and it to my original location," where both destinations are derived from the game state rather than chosen by the player.
Choosing a unit at Azir's current location is legal; the impossible swap is ignored at resolution.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Gangplank, Naval replaces one part of a spell or ability, does the rest still resolve?
explanation:
Yes.
A replacement effect only replaces the specific event or instruction that qualifies for it. Rule 370.1
For Gangplank, that means a stun, might decrease, or return to hand caused by a spell or ability that chose him.

 A player plays Star-Crossed, targeting their own Empowered Gangplank as the friendly unit and an opponent's Elder Dragon as the enemy unit.

 Returning Elder Dragon doesn't choose Gangplank, so his replacement effect has nothing to apply to there — it's returned to hand as normal.
 Returning Gangplank is the qualifying event: instead of going to hand, he gets +3 might.
 The rest of Star-Crossed resolves normally; it simply produces a different result for the one instruction that involves Gangplank.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell target a unit that died from the same event?
explanation:
Yes, because targets are not chosen until the ability is finalized — by which point all units that died in the same event are already in the trash.

Whenever a unit with Deathknell dies, its trigger is placed on the chain as a pending item. Rule 808.1.d.2
