During a cleanup, this ordering is enforced system-wide: step 3a queues all Deathknell triggers from every unit with lethal damage Rule 323.4 and only then does step 3b move those units to the trash. Rule 323.5

The same result applies when one kill instruction kills multiple units.
Their deaths are simultaneous because they result from the same game action, Rule 370.1.a.2 and each relevant Deathknell becomes pending before its unit moves to the trash. Rule 428.1.a.1.b Rule 808.1.d.2

In either case, all units that died from that event are in the trash before the pending ability is finalized and its target is chosen. Rule 334.2 Rule 355.8

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell play a unit to the battlefield where he died?
explanation:
Yes, as long as you controlled that battlefield when Glasc Mixologist died.

Outside a showdown, the Deathknell trigger remains on the chain as a pending item from the moment it is queued.
Because a chain exists, the turn remains in a closed state, Rule 309.1 and cleanup step 4 — which makes unoccupied battlefields uncontrolled — only applies during an open state. Rule 323.6
The battlefield stays under your control, so when the unit is finalized you can choose it as a valid destination. Rule 355.2.a

During a showdown, control of the battlefield cannot change until instructed by the steps of the combat or showdown, Rule 190.4.b so the question does not arise.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens when Glasc Mixologist is my only defender and his Deathknell plays a unit where he died?
explanation:
Several things here commonly catch players off guard: surviving enemy units heal to full before the new unit arrives, neither player wins the original combat, and a second combat immediately follows.

The combat cleanup heals all units before any pending trigger can resolve, Rule 466.1.a.1 Rule 334 so by the time Glasc's Deathknell finalizes and the new unit reaches the battlefield, the enemy is already back to full health.
Because Glasc was your only defender, no defenders remain during cleanup step 3d, so the surviving attackers are not recalled. Rule 466.1.a.2

With units from both players now present, combat result is determined.
Because both players have units there, the result is "No Result." Rule 466.3.d
A fresh combat is immediately staged at that battlefield. Rule 466.3.d.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Heedless Resurrection is countered, is the killed unit returned?
explanation:
No, as the kill is an additional cost and countering a spell never refunds costs already paid.

Killing a friendly unit is an additional cost required to play Heedless Resurrection.
A countered spell does nothing and is cleared from the chain. Rule 425.1.a
Countering does not refund any costs paid to play a card, including additional costs. Rule 425.1.c Rule 425.1.c.1
That cost is paid before the spell resolves, so the killed unit is not returned.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I kill a unit with Heedless Resurrection's cost and then resurrect that same unit?
explanation:
No, as the resurrection target must already be in your trash when you choose it, before the kill cost is paid.

When playing Heedless Resurrection, you must choose the unit to resurrect during step 2 of finalization — the "Make relevant choices" step. Rule 355.5
At that point, the unit you intend to kill is still on the board, not yet in your trash.
"A unit from your trash" must be in your trash to be a valid target, Rule 355.9.a so a living unit on the board cannot be chosen.
The additional cost — killing a friendly unit — is paid in step 4, Rule 357.2 after all choices are already locked in. Rule 355.15

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Heedless Resurrection's "ignoring its cost" instruction also ignore the resurrected unit's additional costs, such as Accelerate?
explanation:
No.
"Ignoring its cost" only sets the resurrected unit's base energy and power costs to zero; additional costs are not waived.

When Heedless Resurrection instructs you to play a unit from your trash "ignoring its cost," that instruction sets the resurrected unit's base energy cost and base power cost to zero. Rule 356.1.b.1
Additional costs — such as the optional Accelerate cost — are applied in a separate step after the base cost is zeroed out and are unaffected by the "ignoring its cost" instruction. Rule 356.1.b.3
If the resurrected unit has an optional additional cost you may choose whether to pay it; Rule 356.2.b.1 if it has a mandatory additional cost you must pay it. Rule 356.2.a.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Heedless Resurrection gains Repeat, do I need to kill a friendly unit for each repetition?
explanation:
No.
The additional cost to kill a friendly unit is paid once, as part of playing the spell.

Additional costs like this are paid during step 4 of playing the card, Rule 357.2 not during resolution.
Repeat makes the spell's instructions execute an additional time upon resolution, Rule 820.1.d.1 but does not re-run costs that were already paid while playing — "as you play me" instructions execute once, before the Repeat execution ever occurs. Rule 135.2.b.3

No matter how many times Repeat is paid, the spell is only played once, Rule 820.3.a so you kill only one friendly unit.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Hidden Blade's kill is replaced, does the target's controller draw?
explanation:
Yes.
Replacing Hidden Blade's kill does not prevent its linked draw instruction from executing.

The phrase "its controller" links the draw to the unit affected by the preceding kill instruction. Rule 359.3.e.14
Replacing that kill action does not stop the later linked instruction unless it directly references the action itself. Rule 359.3.e.14.b
Hidden Blade's draw references the targeted unit's controller, not whether the unit was killed, so the draw still executes.

 You play Hidden Blade targeting an opponent's unit.
 They respond with Zhonya's Hourglass, which replaces the unit's death.
 The unit is not killed.
 Because it was still a legal target when Hidden Blade resolved, the opponent draws 2.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Hidden Blade's target becomes illegal, does that target's controller draw?
explanation:
No.
An illegal target is entirely unaffected by the spell, and the draw is no exception.

An illegal target is unaffected by the spell, so Hidden Blade's kill instruction is ignored. Rule 359.3.e.5
When an earlier linked instruction is ignored, its later linked instructions are also ignored, so the controller does not draw. Rule 359.3.e.14.a

 You play Hidden Blade targeting an opponent's unit at a battlefield.
 They respond by moving it to their base using Flash.
 Hidden Blade resolves.
 The unit is no longer at a battlefield, so it is an illegal target.
 The unit is not killed and the opponent does not draw.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If I target Irelia, Fervent with a spell or ability and it gets countered, does she still get +1 might?
explanation:
Yes.

Irelia is chosen as a target during step 2 of playing the spell or ability — the "Make relevant choices" step. Rule 355.5 Rule 355.7
This happens before the spell or ability is finalized on the chain and before opponents have any opportunity to react.
After the spell or ability finishes finalizing, her targeting effect is added to the chain as a pending item. Rule 383.4.b.2 Rule 383.4.b.3
That trigger is finalized before opponents receive an opportunity to react. Rule 337.3 Rule 337.4
The trigger is not contingent on the spell or ability that caused it successfully resolving.
Countering the spell or ability only prevents it from resolving Rule 425.1.a — it has no bearing on Irelia's already-triggered ability.

 Blade Dancer works the same way.
 Her triggered ability reads "When you choose a friendly unit, you may exhaust me and pay Universal to ready it."
 It ends up on the chain before the original spell can be countered.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Blade Dancer's ability trigger Irelia, Fervent's +1 might?
explanation:
Not from choosing — but she can still trigger from being readied if she was exhausted.

Blade Dancer does not choose a unit — it does not target. Rule 355.10.d Rule 355.10.d.1
"It" in "ready it" deterministically refers back to the unit already identified as Blade Dancer's trigger condition, with no separate choice made by the player.
Irelia's ability can only trigger from Blade Dancer if she was exhausted and is readied by it — and only through the readying half of her ability, not the choosing half. Rule 415.1

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Irelia, Fervent get +1 might when she readies during the Awaken Phase?
explanation:
Yes, but only if she was exhausted and actually transitions to the ready state.

During the Awaken Phase at the start of each turn, the turn player readies all game objects they control that are able to be readied. Rule 315.1.b
Readying is the action of marking a game object as available for action. Rule 415.1
If Irelia was exhausted, she transitions to ready and her trigger fires.

If she is already ready at the start of your turn, she cannot be readied again Rule 415.1.b — no readying event occurs and the trigger does not fire.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a Repeat spell targeting Irelia, Fervent for both instructions give her +1 might twice?
explanation:
Yes, as choosing her for each instruction is a separate triggering event.

Repeat is functionally "execute the spell's instructions one additional time". Rule 820.1.d
When the Repeat cost is paid, choices for both executions are made during the same "Make relevant choices" step of playing the card. Rule 820.2 Rule 820.2.a
Choosing Irelia for the first instruction and choosing her for the second target her twice.
After the spell finalizes, her targeting effect is added to the chain as a pending item once for each targeting event. Rule 383.4.b.2 Rule 383.4.b.3

 You play Feral Strength and pay its Repeat cost, choosing Irelia for both instructions.
 After Feral Strength finalizes, Irelia's ability triggers twice — once per targeting event — and both triggers are added to the chain.
 When her triggers resolve, she receives +1 and +1 from her own ability.
 When the spell resolves, Irelia receives +2 and +2 from the spell's two instructions.
 That's +6 might total this turn.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If I move Irresistible Faefolk to an open battlefield and pull an enemy unit there, who is the attacker?
explanation:
You — the Irresistible Faefolk player — are the attacker.

When Irresistible Faefolk moves to an open (uncontrolled) battlefield, that move applies the contested status to the battlefield. Rule 450 Rule 190.3.a
Irresistible Faefolk's trigger resolves after the cleanup caused by its own move, moving the enemy unit to that battlefield.
During the cleanup following the enemy unit's move, combat is staged because opposing units are now present at the contested battlefield. Rule 319.8 Rule 323.9
When combat opens, the attacker is defined as the player whose unit(s) applied the contested status. Rule 464.2.c.1
That is you — the player who moved Irresistible Faefolk.
The opponent whose unit was pulled in is the defender. Rule 464.2.c.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If I play Irresistible Faefolk directly to a battlefield, does its ability trigger?
explanation:
No — playing a unit to a battlefield is not a move, so the ability does not trigger.

A move is defined as a permanent changing its position from one location on the board to another. Rule 446.1
Playing a card involves it entering the board from a non-board zone (such as your hand), which is a zone change, not a move. Rule 446.2
Because Irresistible Faefolk's ability specifically triggers when it *moves* to a battlefield, playing it directly there does not satisfy that trigger condition.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If an opponent responds to my move trigger by removing Irresistible Faefolk from the battlefield, does the enemy unit still move?
explanation:
Yes — the enemy unit still moves to that battlefield.

Irresistible Faefolk's trigger condition is moving to a battlefield, and "that battlefield" in the effect is a referent to the battlefield named in that trigger condition.
Information referenced from a trigger condition is checked when the trigger condition is fulfilled, not when the ability resolves. Rule 359.3.f.3
That means "that battlefield" was already fixed the moment Irresistible Faefolk moved there and placed the ability on the chain.

Suppose an opponent responds to the triggered ability by playing Gust (or similarly, Star-Crossed), targeting Irresistible Faefolk itself to return it to your hand.
Irresistible Faefolk returns to your hand, but the triggered ability is unaffected — it's already an independent item on the chain, and the battlefield it references was fixed at trigger time.
When it resolves, it moves an enemy unit to that battlefield, even though Irresistible Faefolk is no longer there.

This differs from information derived from an ability's source or targets, which is generally checked when the referencing instruction executes and may become unavailable before resolution. Rule 359.3.f.1 Rule 359.3.f.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Karthus, Eternal's ability apply if he dies from the same effect as the unit with Deathknell?
explanation:
Yes, because Deathknell triggers are always queued as pending items before the dying unit leaves the board.

Whenever a unit with Deathknell is killed — whether by a kill effect or by lethal damage during cleanup — its trigger is added to the chain before the card is moved to the trash. Rule 808.1.d.2
Karthus's passive is only active while he is on the board. Rule 365.1
When one kill action kills Karthus and another unit simultaneously, as with The Ruination, Karthus is still present when that unit's Deathknell triggers. Rule 370.1.a.2
In the cleanup case this ordering is enforced explicitly: step 3a queues all Deathknell triggers Rule 323.4 before step 3b moves any of those units to the trash. Rule 323.5

 You control Karthus and a friendly unit with Deathknell.
 Your opponent plays The Ruination, which kills all units.
 Both are sent to the trash, but not before Karthus's ability doubles the Deathknell trigger.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a single Not So Fast counter both Deathknell triggers when Karthus, Eternal is on the board?
explanation:
No.
If both Deathknell triggers are legal targets for Not So Fast, one copy can counter only one of them.

When a friendly unit with Deathknell dies while Karthus is on the board, his ability causes that Deathknell to trigger an additional time.
Each trigger is added to the chain as its own independent pending item. Rule 808.1.d.2
Not So Fast targets a single spell or ability, so each copy can counter only one trigger.

This applies only when the Deathknell ability chooses one of your friendly units or gear.
Otherwise, Not So Fast cannot target either trigger.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Kennen grant Flow to a spell put into the trash by Minefield's ability triggered by the same conquer?
explanation:
No.
Kennen's conquer ability must choose a spell already in your trash when the ability is finalized on the chain. Rule 355.5 Rule 355.8

Kennen's ability and Minefield's ability trigger from the same conquer and are added to the chain as pending items. Rule 383.3.d
Regardless of their order, every pending item must be finalized before any item can begin resolving. Rule 337.3 Rule 337.4
Minefield therefore cannot put its two cards into your trash until after Kennen has chosen a spell, and that choice cannot later be changed. Rule 355.15

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Lacerate target a unit with more than 3 might?
explanation:
Yes, Lacerate can target any otherwise legal unit, regardless of its might.

"Choose a unit" targets a unit, Rule 355.7 Rule 355.9.a and adds no might-based targeting restriction — "unit" only identifies the category of game object being targeted. Rule 355.9.a.1
The instruction to kill it "if it has 3 might or less" is not part of the target description at all — it's a condition checked on the effect itself as Lacerate resolves.
This is unlike a card such as Gust, which reads "Return a unit at a battlefield with 3 might or less to its owner's hand" — there, "with 3 might or less" describes the target, so it's a genuine targeting restriction and only such units are valid choices. Rule 355.9.b

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If my opponent targets my spell with Lilting Lullaby and I counter my own spell in response, can I still play spells?
explanation:
Yes.
Countering your own spell removes it from the chain, so Lilting Lullaby has no valid target when it resolves — and with nothing to counter, the linked restriction on playing spells is also ignored.

When you counter your own spell, it is cleared from the chain. Rule 425.1.a
"Spell" in a targeting context refers to objects on the chain. Rule 355.9.a.2
By the time Lilting Lullaby resolves, its target is no longer on the chain and no longer meets the targeting requirements — this is mistargeting. Rule 359.3.e.2 Rule 359.3.e.9

Because all of Lilting Lullaby's first instruction's targets are now invalid, the "Counter a spell" instruction does not execute. Rule 359.3.e.7

"Counter a spell" and "Its controller can't play spells this turn" are linked instructions — the second references the controller of the spell from the first.
Since the earlier linked instruction was ignored, the later one is ignored as well. Rule 359.3.e.14.a

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I use Lux, Crownguard's ability to pay for Hard Bargain?
explanation:
No.
Lux's ability can add energy to pay a spell's costs while that spell is being played, but it cannot supply the energy demanded by Hard Bargain.

Paying a spell's costs is part of the process of playing it.
During that step, its controller can activate Reaction abilities that add resources to pay those costs. Rule 357.1 Rule 357.1.a
Once the spell is finalized on the chain, its costs have already been paid and opponents receive an opportunity to play reactions. Rule 359.3.a Rule 359.3.c

Hard Bargain's instruction, "Counter a spell unless its controller pays <Energy value={2} />," is executed later, when Hard Bargain resolves. Rule 158.1
That payment is not a cost of playing the targeted spell.
Although abilities that add resources can normally be activated whenever a spell or ability requires resources to be paid, Lux restricts her added energy to playing spells. Rule 429.3
It therefore cannot be used for Hard Bargain's payment or for another payment required while a spell or ability resolves.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Disarming Rake kill Dazzling Aurora if both are chosen with Promising Future?
explanation:
Yes, regardless of which card is put on the chain first.

Disarming Rake's "When you play me" ability is a play effect.
It is added to the chain as a separate pending item only after Disarming Rake finalizes and enters the board. Rule 383.4.a Rule 383.4.a.2

If Dazzling Aurora finalized first, it is already on the board.
If Disarming Rake finalized first, its play effect is put on the chain after Dazzling Aurora, so the older Dazzling Aurora finalizes and enters before the play effect does. Rule 337.1.b Rule 337.2
In either order, Dazzling Aurora is on the board when Disarming Rake's play effect is finalized and can be killed by it.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Ravenbloom Prefect banish Dazzling Aurora if both are chosen with Promising Future?
explanation:
Only if Ravenbloom Prefect finalizes before Dazzling Aurora.

Unlike Disarming Rake's own play effect, Ravenbloom Prefect's ability triggers when another object is played. Rule 383.4.a.4
Ravenbloom Prefect must therefore be on the board when Dazzling Aurora finishes being played for its trigger condition to be fulfilled. Rule 383.2.c Rule 419.4.a

If Ravenbloom Prefect finalizes first, it enters the board before Dazzling Aurora finalizes, so its ability triggers and can banish Dazzling Aurora.
If Dazzling Aurora finalizes first, Ravenbloom Prefect is still a pending card on the chain when Aurora enters, so the ability does not trigger later when Prefect enters.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When do I choose whether to pay the power for Rebuttal?
explanation:
You choose whether to pay Universal when Rebuttal resolves because the optional payment is a cost within the spell's instructions, not an additional cost to play it.

When Rebuttal is finalized, you choose the spell with energy cost no more than <Energy value={4} />. Rule 355.5
The optional power payment is not an additional cost to play Rebuttal; it is a cost within the spell's instructions. Rule 204.2 Rule 204.3
Costs within a spell's instructions are paid during that spell's resolution. Rule 204.3.b

Opponents can therefore react to Rebuttal knowing which spell it chose, but without knowing whether you will pay Universal to gain control of that spell or decline to pay and counter it.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Rebuttal redirect a spell played from Hidden to another location?
explanation:
No — taking control of the spell and making new choices for it does not remove the targeting restriction imposed by Hidden.

Rebuttal allows its controller to remake a finalized spell's targets, Rule 752.1 but every new choice must still be legal. Rule 753.1
When a spell is played from Hidden, its targets must be chosen from among the options at the battlefield where it was hidden unless the spell's own targeting restriction makes that impossible. Rule 811.1.d.2
Changing the spell's controller does not change where it was played from, so this restriction continues to apply.

 An opponent plays Hidden Blade from Hidden and chooses a unit at that battlefield.
 If you gain control of Hidden Blade with Rebuttal, you may choose another legal unit at the same battlefield.
 You cannot choose a unit at another battlefield, and you cannot choose a unit at base because Hidden Blade itself requires a unit "at a battlefield."

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Whose "when you play a spell" abilities trigger for a spell Rebuttal takes control of?
explanation:
The abilities controlled by the spell's new controller trigger because the act of playing the spell is completed when it resolves under that player's control.

Abilities such as Ravenbloom Student's do not trigger when a spell is first placed on or finalized to the chain.
They trigger when the act of playing that spell is completed by its resolution. Rule 419.4.a
At that point, the player who gained control of the spell with Rebuttal is its controller. Rule 191.2

 You control Ravenbloom Student and use Rebuttal to gain control of an opponent's Gust.
 Your Student triggers when Rebuttal resolves.
 When Gust resolves afterward, your Student triggers again because you now control Gust.
 Your opponent's "when you play a spell" abilities do not trigger for Gust.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Do I draw a card if I take control of Back Off?
explanation:
No — you did not play Back Off from your hand merely by taking control of it.

To play a card, a player places it on the chain and queues it for finalization. Rule 419.1
Back Off's "if you played this from your hand" clause is a non-triggered condition, so it checks whether the card was finalized by that player. Rule 419.4.b Rule 329.3
Gaining control of an already-finalized spell does not repeat that process or change which player performed it.

When Back Off resolves under your control, "you" refers to you, but you did not play it from your hand, so you do not draw a card.
The opponent who originally played Back Off does not draw either because they no longer control the resolving spell.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Ruined Rex's Deathknell deal damage before or after units are healed at the end of combat?
explanation:
After.
The combat heal is part of the same cleanup that queues the trigger, and the trigger does not resolve until that cleanup has run to completion.

When Ruined Rex dies with lethal damage during a combat cleanup, the steps run in this order:

1. Step 3a — Ruined Rex's Deathknell trigger is added to the chain as a pending item. Rule 323.4 Rule 808.1.d.2
2. Step 3b — Ruined Rex is moved to the trash. Rule 323.5
3. Step 3c — All units are healed.
This step is inserted by the combat special cleanup. Rule 466.1.a.1

The pending trigger does not begin finalization until the cleanup task is complete. Rule 334
After the cleanup, the trigger is finalized and its target is chosen.
Once no pending items remain, players receive priority before the trigger resolves. Rule 337.4
If it is not countered, it eventually resolves and deals 4 damage to the chosen enemy unit.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Ruined Rex's Deathknell target the Mech tokens created by Ferrous Forerunner's Deathknell, if both die at the same time?
explanation:
No.
Ruined Rex chooses its target before Ferrous Forerunner creates its Mech tokens.

When both units die in the same cleanup, their Deathknell abilities become pending items. Rule 323.4
All pending items are finalized before players receive priority and ordinary abilities begin resolving. Rule 337.3 Rule 337.4

Ruined Rex chooses its target during finalization, Rule 355.5 while Ferrous Forerunner creates its Mechs only when its ability resolves.
Regardless of finalization order, those Mechs do not exist when Rex chooses its target.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Sacrifice is countered, is the killed unit returned?
explanation:
No, as the kill is an additional cost and countering a spell never refunds costs already paid.

Killing a friendly Mighty unit is an additional cost required to play Sacrifice.
A countered spell does nothing and is cleared from the chain. Rule 425.1.a
Countering does not refund any costs paid to play a card, including additional costs. Rule 425.1.c Rule 425.1.c.1
That cost is paid before the spell resolves, so the killed unit is not returned.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can my opponent interact before the Mighty unit chosen for Sacrifice's additional cost is killed?
explanation:
No normal reaction window opens between choosing the Mighty unit and killing it.

The unit killed as a cost is not a target — objects referenced as part of a cost are explicitly excluded from targeting. Rule 355.10.c

Costs are paid during step 4 of finalization, and finalization does not pass priority. Rule 357.2 Rule 337.1.a
During that step, Sacrifice's controller may activate an eligible Add ability with Reaction when resources are required, even without priority. Rule 357.1.a Rule 429.3 Rule 429.3.a
This limited exception does not create a normal reaction window or permit an opponent to play a spell like Stupefy between choosing and killing the unit.

By the time a normal priority window opens, the cost has been paid and the unit is already in the trash.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Shadow Assassin count itself when I play it from my trash?
explanation:
No.
Playing Shadow Assassin from your trash moves it onto the chain first, Rule 354 Rule 419.1 so by the time it enters, it's no longer in your trash.
It enters ready only if a *different* copy of it is still there.

Consuming Curse and Shadowblade Lurker work the same way.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: When I play Shadowblade Lurker from my trash, does it discount its own cost?
explanation:
No.
Playing Shadowblade Lurker from your trash moves it onto the chain first, Rule 354 Rule 419.1 so it's no longer in your trash when its cost is worked out.
Only the *other* copies still in your trash reduce the cost.

Consuming Curse and Shadow Assassin work the same way.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a Reflection token with Temporary lose Temporary after Shady Spectacles makes it a copy of a unit that doesn't have Temporary?
explanation:
No.
It keeps the Temporary keyword granted to it separately, even if Shady Spectacles makes it a copy of a unit without Temporary.

Deceiver and Mirror Image first play a Reflection token, then make it a copy, and then grant it Temporary.
The keyword therefore comes from a separate effect rather than from the traits copied by the token.

Shady Spectacles' "becomes a copy of that unit" applies in the trait-altering layer, Rule 477.1.b Rule 477.1.b.1 while the separate keyword grant applies afterward in the ability-altering layer. Rule 477.2 Rule 477.2.a
The rules' Reflection example likewise confirms that copied Reflection tokens retain Temporary. Rule 477.1.b.1.b
Because the grant has no stated duration, it continues for as long as the token remains on the board. Rule 801.3.a.3

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Guardian Angel, Zhonya's Hourglass, or Tactical Retreat save a unit from Smite?
explanation:
Yes.
These effects can prevent the banish because the unit's controller decides which replacement effect applies first and can apply their protective effect before Smite's.

Smite's "if it would die this turn, banish it instead" is a replacement effect. Rule 369.1
So are each of the three protective effects, which all replace the event of a unit dying.
When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the controller of the affected unit decides the order they apply. Rule 372

If the unit's controller applies their protective effect first, the death event is fully replaced — the unit is healed, exhausted, and recalled, or an equipment dies in its place. Rule 370.1.a.1
A replacement effect can only be applied once to an event, and to any events that replace it; Rule 370.2 once the death event has been consumed, Smite's replacement effect has no qualifying event left to intercept, and the unit is not banished.

Conversely, if Smite's effect is applied first, the unit is banished.
The protective effects each replace a "die" event — since banishment is not a subset of killing, Rule 427.2.a none of them can chain onto the resulting "banish" event.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Sunken Temple trigger if I conquer with a unit that is only Mighty due to Assault?
explanation:
Yes, Sunken Temple will trigger even if the unit is only Mighty because of the bonus might it gained from Assault. Rule 807.1.c Rule 807.1.d.1

Control is established and the conquer occurs Rule 466.5.d before attacker and defender designations are removed. Rule 466.7.a
This means units still have their attacker designation — and therefore Assault active — at the time the conquer trigger is evaluated. Rule 708 Rule 710

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: How does Switcheroo work?
explanation:
Switcheroo does not swap might values directly — it determines the difference in current might at resolution and applies +X/-X modifiers accordingly.

Switcheroo uses the Swap action, Rule 433 which calculates the difference between the two units' current might, then applies a -X modifier to the higher might unit and a +X modifier to the lower might unit.
Current might means the unit's total might at resolution time, including all active modifiers: equipment bonuses, battlefield passives, conditional abilities, and any other effects.
The modifiers Switcheroo applies persist until end of turn.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Switcheroo result in negative might?
explanation:
Yes.
When referenced by spells or abilities and when summing combat damage, negative might is treated as 0, but might increases and decreases use the actual negative value.

Units can end up with negative might when modifiers included in their current might at resolution are later removed.
Units with might less than 0 are treated as having 0 might when referenced by spells and abilities, and when summing might to be assigned as damage in the Combat Damage Step. Rule 143.2.b
Units with 0 or negative might do not automatically die — units are only killed during cleanup if they have lethal damage, meaning non-zero damage equal to or exceeding their might. Rule 323.5 Rule 142.4.b

If a unit later gains additional might modifiers, they add to the actual negative value.

 A unit at -2 might is targeted with Punch First, which reads "Give a unit +5 Might this turn."
 The unit ends up with 3 might — the +5 modifier adds to the actual -2 value.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can Temporal Breach banish a unit at a different battlefield if played from Hidden?
explanation:
No, when Temporal Breach is played from Hidden, the unit it banishes must be chosen from among units at the battlefield where it was hidden.

"Banish a unit" chooses a specific game object to affect, making it a target, declared as Temporal Breach is put on the chain. Rule 355.5 Rule 355.7 Rule 355.8
Choices made while playing a card from Hidden are restricted to the battlefield where it was hidden. Rule 811.1.d
Specifically, if a Hidden spell chooses any targets, those targets must be chosen from among options at that battlefield, unless the ability explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes this impossible. Rule 811.1.d.2
Temporal Breach's own wording doesn't restrict its target to a location, so this Hidden restriction applies in full — a unit at another battlefield, or in base, isn't a legal target when it's played from Hidden.

If Temporal Breach is played normally, the Hidden restriction does not apply.
It may target an otherwise legal unit at any board location, including a base or battlefield. Rule 811.3

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a unit replayed by Temporal Breach keep temporary modifications or statuses?
explanation:
No, the replayed unit does not keep temporary modifications or statuses it had before Temporal Breach banished it.

Banishment is a non-board zone, Rule 056.1 and a game object that changes zones to or from a non-board zone becomes a new object for tracking purposes. Rule 124
When the unit enters banishment, all temporary modifications and statuses on it are cleared. Rule 124.1
This means effects such as Stupefy's might reduction no longer apply, and a unit that was Empowered is no longer Empowered when it is replayed. Rule 124.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens to equipment attached to a unit replayed by Temporal Breach?
explanation:
The equipment detaches and remains at the unit's previous location because Temporal Breach moves the unit from the board to banishment.

When Temporal Breach moves the unit from the board to banishment, all cards attached to that unit detach and remain at the unit's previous location. Rule 719.5 Rule 435.4.b
The replayed unit is a new game object, Rule 124 and nothing instructs the equipment to attach to it again.

If the unit was at a battlefield, the unattached equipment is recalled to its controller's base during the next cleanup. Rule 435.4.a
If the unit was at a base, the equipment instead remains unattached at that base.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does a replayed unit trigger its attack or defend ability again during the same combat?
explanation:
Yes, if the unit is replayed to the battlefield where combat is in progress, its attack or defend ability can trigger again because it becomes a new game object.

The unit becomes a new game object when it enters banishment, Rule 124 and that new object has not yet had its attack or defend trigger condition checked during that combat.
After the replayed unit enters the battlefield, the next cleanup gives it the same attacker or defender designation as its controller. Rule 323.2.a
Gaining that designation causes its corresponding attack or defend ability to trigger. Rule 383.4.e Rule 383.4.f
The normal once-per-combat limit does not prevent this trigger because it applied to the previous game object, not the newly replayed one. Rule 383.4.e.2.a Rule 383.4.f.2.a

 Ahri, Inquisitive's "When I attack or defend" ability can trigger when she gains the defender designation at the start of combat.
 After that ability resolves, Temporal Breach can banish and replay her to the same battlefield.
 The replayed Ahri is a new game object and gains the defender designation during the next cleanup, triggering her ability a second time in the same combat.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Ravenbloom Conservatory trigger again if Temporal Breach replays my only defending unit?
explanation:
No, Ravenbloom Conservatory does not trigger a second time because it remains the same game object, and its defend trigger has already checked its condition during that combat.

Ravenbloom Conservatory's "When you defend here" ability is a defend trigger whose condition is fulfilled when its controller gains the defender designation. Rule 383.4.f
When combat opens, the defending player and their units separately gain that designation, Rule 464.2.c.3 so Ravenbloom Conservatory checks its trigger condition then.
A defend triggered ability can have its condition checked only once per combat. Rule 383.4.f.2.a

Temporal Breach makes the replayed unit a new game object, Rule 124 which allows that new unit's own defend ability to receive its first condition check during the same combat.
It does not make Ravenbloom Conservatory a new object or begin a new combat, so Ravenbloom Conservatory's ability does not receive another condition check.
The defending player also keeps the defender designation until combat ends, Rule 466.7.a and therefore does not gain it again when the replayed unit gains its separate designation during cleanup.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if Temporal Breach banishes a token unit?
explanation:
The token stops existing the moment it's banished, so there's nothing left for its owner to replay.

Temporal Breach puts the token into its owner's banishment, which is a non-board zone. Rule 056.1
Tokens can only exist on the board or the chain — if a token enters any other zone, it ceases to exist immediately upon arriving there. Rule 186 Rule 186.1
So by the time Temporal Breach's "then its owner plays it to the same location" instruction would apply, the token is already gone, and that part of the spell does nothing for it. Rule 055

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Can I pay optional additional costs, like Accelerate, when replaying a unit banished by Temporal Breach?
explanation:
Yes, since the replayed unit still goes through the complete, normal process of playing a card, and "ignoring its cost" only narrows one part of that process — the base cost — leaving everything else, including optional additional costs, unaffected.

"Its owner plays it" instructs the normal process of playing a card — the unit is removed from banishment and put onto the chain as a pending item, Rule 354 Rule 354.2 it isn't placed directly onto the board.
That pending item goes through the full finalization process once it's ready to be finalized, including making relevant choices Rule 355 and determining total cost. Rule 356
Playing a card "ignoring its cost" only sets its base Energy and base Power cost to zero; Rule 356.1.b.1 further additional costs applied in later steps can still raise the total cost back above zero. Rule 356.1.b.3
Accelerate is one such optional additional cost, paid as a player plays the unit with the ability, Rule 805.2 so its owner may still declare their intent to pay it during finalization Rule 356.2.b.1 and pay it as usual, unaffected by Temporal Breach ignoring the unit's base cost.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if the replayed unit has a mandatory additional cost its owner can't pay?
explanation:
The attempted play is cancelled, and the unit returns to its owner's banishment.

Temporal Breach's instruction to play the unit "ignoring its cost" sets only its base Energy and base Power cost to zero. Rule 356.1.b.1
Mandatory additional costs must still be paid to complete playing the unit. Rule 356.1.b.3 Rule 356.2.a.1
If the owner can't pay one, the unit fails the check that all costs were paid, so the actions taken during its play process are undone and the play is cancelled. Rule 358.2 Rule 358.5
This rewind returns the unit from the chain, Rule 354 to banishment; it does not undo Temporal Breach's earlier, completed instruction that banished it.

 If Temporal Breach banishes Cruel Patron and its owner has no other friendly unit, they can't pay Cruel Patron's mandatory additional cost to kill a friendly unit.
 Cruel Patron cannot finish finalizing and returns to its owner's banishment.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If the unit banished by Temporal Breach has Hidden, can its owner hide it instead of playing it?
explanation:
No, hiding the unit does not fulfill Temporal Breach's instruction to play it.

Hide is a separate action, not a subset of play. Rule 811.1.c.1
Playing the unit puts it on the chain and queues it for finalization, Rule 419.1 whereas hiding would put it facedown at a battlefield. Rule 421.1
Moreover, the unit is in banishment when its owner is instructed to play it, and Hidden only permits a card to be hidden from hand or the champion zone. Rule 811.1.b
Hiding is therefore not an alternative to the instructed play.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: If Temporal Breach banishes and replays my only unit at a battlefield, can I score there on my opponent's turn?
explanation:
No, as control of the battlefield is never lost during this sequence.

When Temporal Breach resolves, the replayed unit is added to the chain as a pending item, Rule 354.2 with its play process held until the spell has fully resolved. Rule 354.3
Once the spell finishes resolving, a cleanup runs — but the pending unit keeps the chain alive throughout it. Rule 330 Rule 331
Because the chain is not empty, the turn remains in a closed state, and cleanup step 4 — which would make the battlefield uncontrolled — only applies during an open state. Rule 190.4.c Rule 323.6
Control is never lost, so there is no opportunity to score a point. Rule 469.1
When all outstanding tasks are complete, the pending unit is finalized Rule 334.2 Rule 337.1 and replayed to the same battlefield you still control, as dictated by Temporal Breach's own text. Rule 359.2

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if Temporal Breach banishes a unit at Rockfall Path?
explanation:
Temporal Breach banishes the unit, but its owner cannot play it back to Rockfall Path.
The unit remains in its owner's banishment.

Rockfall Path prevents the instructed play action.
This does not stop Temporal Breach from resolving; when it reaches the replay instruction, that game action is skipped as impossible. Rule 358.3.a
The earlier banish instruction is unaffected, so the unit remains banished.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: What happens if Brynhir Thundersong prevents the owner of a unit banished by Temporal Breach from playing cards?
explanation:
The unit remains banished.

If Brynhir Thundersong's play effect has resolved, opponents cannot play cards for the rest of that turn.
Temporal Breach can still banish an opponent's unit, but that opponent cannot perform the instruction to play it back.

This does not stop Temporal Breach from resolving.
The replay is an impossible game action and is skipped, Rule 358.3.a just as it is when Rockfall Path prevents the unit from being played to its previous location.
Because the earlier banish instruction was completed normally, the unit remains in its owner's banishment.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Vex, Apathetic's triggered ability target the unit that was just played?
explanation:
No, as the unit to be stunned is determined automatically, so no targeting ever occurs.

When Vex's ability triggers, the unit to be stunned is determined automatically — it is always and only the unit the opponent just played.
Because no choice is ever made about which unit is stunned, the unit is not a target. Rule 355.10.d

This means targeting protection — such as "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities" — offers no defense against the stun.
Deflect similarly does not become relevant, since Deflect is only added to a spell or ability's cost when it targets an opponent's permanent, Rule 809.1.d which is not the case here.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Do opponents have to pay resources to play cards from Hidden while Vex, Cheerless is in combat?
explanation:
Yes, cards played from Hidden by your opponents still cost <Energy value={1} />Universal when Vex is in combat.

When a card with Hidden is played from its facedown state, it is played "ignoring its base cost". Rule 811.1.b
During step 3 of playing a card ("Determine Total Cost"), the following happens in order:

1. Set base costs to zero. Rule 356.1
If an ability or instruction allows you to "ignore" costs, set the base costs to zero.
Hidden cards played from facedown have their base cost set to <Energy value={0} />.
2. Apply cost increases. Rule 356.3
Vex's ability increases enemy spell costs by <Energy value={1} />Universal, which is applied to the total cost even though the base cost is zero.
3. Apply discounts. Rule 356.4
No discounts apply in this scenario.

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)

paraphrases: Does Vex, Cheerless reduce Deflect costs when you play spells?
explanation:
Yes, the cost reduction applies to Deflect costs when you target an opponent's permanent while she's in combat.

Deflect is a mandatory additional cost. Rule 356.2.a.2 Rule 809.1.d
When you play a friendly spell that targets an opponent's permanent with Deflect, that additional cost is added before Vex's discount is applied. Rule 356.2 Rule 356.4

Vex's discount can offset resources added by Deflect because discounts can reduce additional costs. Rule 356.4.f
However, her discount cannot reduce the spell's resulting cost below her printed minimum of <Energy value={1} />. Rule 356.4.e

(Source: riftboundfaq.com by Christian I. (Near) and contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/ChristianIvicevic/riftboundfaq)
